title: How a Fireplace Chimney Works in 60 Seconds 🔥🏠 #shorts
description:
A chimney works on one simple idea: hot gas rises. The fire's hot smoke climbs the flue and creates a draft that pulls fresh air into the fire, but it also drags warm room air away, which is why an open fireplace loses most of its heat. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#fireplace #chimney #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: An open fireplace can send over *90%* of its heat straight up the chimney.

steps.label: Fire
steps.text: Burning wood makes hot gases and *smoke* that are lighter than the cool air around them.

steps.label: Draft
steps.text: They rise up the flue, creating a *draft* that pulls fresh air into the fire.

steps.label: Heat loss
steps.text: That draft also pulls *warm room air* up the chimney, so most of the heat escapes.

steps.label: Damper
steps.text: A metal *damper* closes the chimney when no fire is burning.

steps.label: Top
steps.text: The chimney rises above the *roof*, so wind carries the smoke away.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Hot air *rises*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
